comment: T4 baseline (docs/TESTING.md). `nodes` counts every node and `retainedNodes` only those carrying a mesh of their own (the Labels). Since P1 all of them draw: `buffersAlive` is 2 whatever the node count - the growing vertex buffer and the fullscreen quad the filter passes draw - because no node owns one any more. It read 3 until the P1 review, and that 3 was a C function returning the literal 3: gated against the literal, so the assertion compared a constant to a constant and would have kept passing if every Label allocated a buffer again. It also miscounted, since the third thing it named was the font image and not a buffer. It is made-minus-freed at the sg_make_buffer/sg_destroy_buffer sites now, and was checked by allocating one extra buffer and watching it read 3, then 2 again, and `vertices` is what proves every label emitted geometry instead of being dropped by a full pool. `ui.draws` is 20000 and not 253 because the bench alternates a white-texture card with a font-texture label on every node; the unified pipeline and the white texel in the glyph atlas that collapse that are P2's. Counters gate hard; milliseconds only report, with a warn threshold, because this is a shared developer box. How much that matters, measured 2026-09-20 after the sampler commit: the same `benchSprites` binary that read 1.63 ms when this file was written reads 1.87-2.09 ms on a box sitting at 54% CPU from other work, which is 1.28x and most of the way to the 1.5x warn. The numbers below were not re-taken to make that go away, and the warn factor was not raised: a threshold moved to fit the reading stops being a threshold. What a millisecond row can answer is *relative* regression, and only one way - build both commits, run them interleaved on the same box in the same minute. Done for the sampler commit against its parent `06c2bd0`: PREV 1.96/2.09/1.87/2.00 against NOW 1.98/1.97/1.92/1.96, mean 1.98 vs 1.96, so guardrail 8 holds and the gap to 1.63 is the machine. A gate WARN on a millisecond row means re-run that A/B, not that the phase regressed — SCENE-SCALE.md:197 records its own numbers being taken at load average 14-17. Keys are nested rather than dotted so tests/bench/check.ms can read them through the JsonValue accessors.

taken.renderer: the display list: one growing vertex buffer, one upload, no per-node sg_buffer
